issues.legal_issue: An appellate or revisional court may order restoration of possession after disposing of an appeal, reference, or revision, provided it exercises that power within a reasonable time.
material_facts: The trial court convicted the accused of trespassing and forcibly taking possession of immovable property, but did not order restoration of possession.
The appellate court upheld the conviction and disposed of the appeal.
Two weeks after the appeal was disposed of, an application for restoration was made to the appellate court, which ordered restoration.
The High Court set aside that order on the ground that restoration could not be ordered after disposal of the appeal.
issues.conclusion: The appellate or revisional court has power to order restoration after disposing of the appeal, reference, or revision; it must exercise that discretion within a reasonable time of the disposal. The restoration order was reinstated.
issues.legal_principle: Section 456(2) of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 applies where a trial court has recorded a conviction but omitted or refused to order restoration, and an appeal or revision has been preferred against the conviction or the refusal. Read with the change from section 522(3) of the 1898 Code, and the Law Commission’s 41st Report, paragraph 43.24, the words “while disposing of” mean in continuation of the disposal and do not require the restoration order to appear in the judgment disposing of the proceeding. Parliament did not impose a fixed limitation on the appellate or revisional court’s power; the court must exercise its discretion within a reasonable time. The judgment discusses Abdul Mannan v. Taiyab Ali, Krishnan Moothan v. V. K. A. Krishnankutty Moothan, Nihal Singh v. Emperor, Basanta Kumar Maity v. Kenaram Maity, Fida Hussain v. Sarfaraz Hussain, and Savlaram Sadoba Navle v. Dhyaneshwar Vishnu Chinke in considering the earlier conflict of views.

rule.if: appeal_or_revision_proceeding and conviction_recorded and trial_court_left_possession_unrestored and appellate_disposition_completed and restoration_sought_within_reasonable_time

predicates.appeal_or_revision_proceeding: The matter is an appeal, reference, or revision arising from a criminal proceeding.
predicates.conviction_recorded: The trial court recorded a conviction.
predicates.trial_court_left_possession_unrestored: The trial court omitted or refused to order restoration of possession of the immovable property.
predicates.appellate_disposition_completed: The appeal, reference, or revision has been disposed of.
predicates.restoration_sought_within_reasonable_tim: Restoration was sought within a reasonable time of the disposal of the appeal, reference, or revision.

issues.definition: When a conviction has been recorded, the trial court has left possession unrestored, and restoration is sought within a reasonable time after an appeal, reference, or revision is disposed of, the appellate or revisional court may order restoration.
